clue.text: Licence to make product for iodine-deficient hospital inmate

indicators.note: something deficient is lacking an element, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a person being treated in hospital
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A permit to manufacture goods for a hospital patient short of iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iodine-deficient' reads as a medical condition, but it tells you to drop the I from PATIENT to leave PATENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A patent is the official right granted to an inventor to produce and sell an invention exclusively.

clue.text: Engineer to help over old hazard for road users

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: letters to rearrange
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A road engineer is needed to fix an old danger to motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' sounds like a person, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in a road surface that can damage vehicles, a danger to drivers.

clue.text: Subject to endless choice

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a pick is a choice

explanation.surface: A subject that faces an unlimited range of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' reads as a phrase meaning liable to; the definition is 'Subject' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter under discussion, a subject.

clue.text: Women upset about stage in monthly cycle

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: its letters rearranged
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Women unhappy about a phase of the menstrual cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the menstrual cycle; the monthly cycle meant is the moon's.
explanation.definitionFit: The new moon is the phase of the lunar month when the moon is invisible, starting each cycle.

clue.text: Virtual image representing oneself as woman meeting sailor

parts.note: a woman's name
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone choosing an online picture of themselves as a woman getting together with a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the graphic figure a user chooses to stand for them in games or online forums.

clue.text: Incredibly naive about northern capital city

indicators.note: something done incredibly is beyond belief, so the letters are mixed up
about means around, so these letters go round another

parts.note: its letters rearranged
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Someone unbelievably innocent about a city in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital of Austria, so it is a capital city.

clue.text: Heartless trader welcomes note by a certain person in charge of the money

definitions.text: person in charge of the money

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in a guest, so other letters are placed inside
without a heart means the central part of the word is cut out

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes
E is a musical note
taken as written
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A dealer with no heart takes in a banknote from someone in charge of the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the heart taken out is the three central letters, not just two. 'note' suggests money, but it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of a club, company or society.

clue.text: Once more assert right to large piece of property

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an estate is an extensive area of land owned by one person

explanation.surface: Someone once again claiming entitlement to a big landholding.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to say again, so to assert something a second time.

clue.text: Reform gambling law, or cause a threat to temperate living?

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: all thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A campaigner's ultimatum: change the betting legislation or bring about a danger to civilised life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temperate living' plays on moderate habits, but it means life in temperate climates.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming, the rise in world temperatures, endangers the climate of temperate regions.

clue.text: Backing favourites a short part of the way

definitions.text: a short part of the way

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a teacher's pets are the favourites

explanation.surface: Supporting the favourite runners only gets you partway, a gambler's lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing favourites' sounds like betting talk; backing is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stride, a short distance covered along a route.

clue.text: Creature found in surprisingly edible stew

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly is not in the expected form, so the letters come out rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An animal unexpectedly discovered in a casserole that turned out to be edible.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is a large African antelope, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Trip on choirboy's cloak

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling over a chorister's robe.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no signal word: the definition sits at the end, and the rest of the clue holds the answer whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like outer garment with a hole for the head, a kind of cloak.

clue.text: A new key used by sergeant major to go into bar with musician

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so these letters sit within another word

parts.note: to bar is to ban
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
D is a musical key
SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major

explanation.surface: A sergeant major uses a fresh key to get into a pub, accompanied by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it means to forbid; the four small pieces sit inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsman is a player in a band, especially a military or brass band, so a musician.

clue.text: Record complication with figure

parts.note: REC is the abbreviation on a recording button
a tangle is a muddle or complication

explanation.surface: A record-keeping problem involving a number in the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a number, but here it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided plane shape with right angles, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Making lacework to cover old, originally oriental, body staining

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping round it, so letters go inside

parts.note: tatting is making lace by knotting thread
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: originally points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Lace-making as a way to hide old body art of Eastern origin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatting is a handmade lace craft using a small shuttle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattooing marks the skin with permanent ink designs, a staining of the body.

clue.text: Plant hidden by giant reeds

indicators.note: something hidden by other words lies concealed within their run of letters

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A plant lost from view among very tall reeds in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a large woody perennial, so it belongs to the plant kingdom.

clue.text: Name of place reported

indicators.note: something reported is spoken out loud, so we want a word that is said the same way

parts.note: a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: The name of a location as given in a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is a verb here, as in naming a source.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to mention or quote something, such as a reference or example, by name.

clue.text: See 17
Author trading in her cocoa tokens?

indicators.note: trading means swapping things around, so these letters exchange places

parts.note: all sixteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A writer cashing in her vouchers for hot chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Cookson was a hugely popular English novelist of working-class life in the North East.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Cookson wrote over a hundred novels, so she is an author.

clue.text: Restraint shown by daughter not sharing in excessive insensibility

indicators.note: not taking part means being left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: hardness of heart is a lack of feeling
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter shows self-control by refusing to join in callous behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness is a set of straps used to hold or control a horse or a person, a restraint.

clue.text: Start to notice a smell developing

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Beginning to detect an odour that is getting stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to notice' reads as a phrase about noticing; 'Start to' selects the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being and beginning to grow.

clue.text: Worm I threw away

indicators.note: threw away suggests scattering, so these letters fly into another order

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An angler's confession about discarding a worm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worm' is a verb, to twist and wriggle, not the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, the way one might worm about.

clue.text: Embroidered initials for American relative accepting organ transplant

indicators.note: a transplant moves things to a new position, so these letters are rearranged
accepting something means taking it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: the American word for mother
its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Personalised stitching ordered for an American mother who has had an organ transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ transplant' reads as surgery; 'transplant' is the anagram signal for the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A monogram is a design of interwoven initials, often stitched onto linen or shirts.

clue.text: Vegetable grown by police officer covered in spots

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A spotty policeman tends his vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a crisp red root eaten raw in salads, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Viking capturing heart of Latin poet

indicators.note: capturing means seizing and holding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the Vikings included Danes

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, which is what is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

explanation.surface: A Norse raider seizing the core of a Roman poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin poet' reads together, but Dante wrote in Italian; 'Latin' only supplies its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy, is Italy's most celebrated poet.

clue.text: Help donkey transporting saint to church

indicators.note: transporting moves things about, so these letters are carried into a new order

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
its letters rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone asks a donkey to carry a holy man to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transporting' looks like the donkey carrying the saint inside it, but it shuffles the word saint itself rather than holding ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is aid or support, the noun matching help.

clue.text: Speaker's massage requirement?

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what is heard, so we want a word sounding like the one indicated

parts.note: to knead is to massage

explanation.surface: A public speaker wanting a massage before going on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something that is necessary, a requirement.

clue.text: Return weapon and receive piece of gold

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to get is to receive

explanation.surface: Hand back your firearm and collect a payment in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of precious metal, especially gold, found in the ground.

clue.text: A religious group embracing party leader's view

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: embracing means hugging or enclosing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A religious faction warmly welcoming a political party leader's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party leader' looks like a politician, but it is just the first letter of party.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a particular outlook or angle, so it can mean a view.
